question.text: Under the Stewardship Code released by SEBI (Circular Nos. CIR/CFD/CMD 1/168/19 dated December 24, 2019 and CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2020/55 dated March 30, 2020), all AIFs are required to:

answer.text: Maintain a 10% minimum voting stake in every listed investee company
Publish every vote cast within 24 hours on the AIF's website
Actively monitor investee companies and vote in important company matters, and have a clear policy for collaboration with other institutional investors
Route all proxy votes through a SEBI-empanelled voting agent

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.2.4.1 and Ch 11.7.1, under SEBI's Stewardship framework, all AIFs are required to actively monitor their investee companies and vote in important company matters. They must have a clear policy for collaboration with other institutional investors to preserve ultimate investors' interests. **The Trap:** There is no 10% minimum voting-stake mandate. Daily public vote disclosure is not required. No SEBI voting-agent mandate exists. **Cross-Exam Context:** Stewardship duty tested in XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) and XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) — XIX-C tests the Manager's responsibility to design the policy. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Publish the stewardship policy on the Manager's website AND incorporate it as a PPM annexure. LPs increasingly screen managers on stewardship maturity — a detailed voting track record is now a fundraising asset.
